_field_contract_.description: Generative contract defining how potential Field candidates are broadly observed and expanded from preserved Business Strategy Domains before any later qualification, normalization, or provenance process.
instruction: Treat a candidate Field as a plausible knowledge, disciplinary, professional, engineering, scientific, technological, or interdisciplinary domain worth preserving for later evaluation.
Prioritize broad candidate coverage over premature precision during this stage.
Generate candidate Fields freely from each BSD without requiring prior academic validation, professional validation, canonical naming, or provenance.
Do not treat BSD naming or BSD membership as proof of Field identity.
Use BSDs as generative observation boundaries rather than as academic classification containers.
Observe candidate Fields independently through all declared observers.
Allow differences in terminology, granularity, disciplinary framing, and interdisciplinary interpretation across observers.
Allow established, emerging, interdisciplinary, convergent, and cross-domain Field candidates to enter the candidate set.
Do not reject a candidate merely because it overlaps with, depends on, or combines knowledge from other Fields.
Allow the same candidate Field to occur under multiple BSD observations without forcing exclusive BSD ownership.
Preserve potentially redundant, overlapping, synonymous, nested, or differently granular candidate expressions for later evaluation.
Do not normalize, merge, rank, validate, canonicalize, or resolve candidate Field identities at this stage.
Do not infer parent-child, hierarchical, nested, or other academic topology among candidate Fields at this stage.

a.description: Observe potential Field candidates through the lens of recognizable disciplinary and educational classification patterns.
a.focus: Discipline-like identities, knowledge-domain boundaries, neighboring domains, and plausible disciplinary expressions.

b.description: Observe potential Field candidates through the lens of academic programs, curricula, educational structures, and bodies of knowledge.
b.focus: Potential curricular identities, educational domains, bodies of knowledge, and independently teachable areas.

c.description: Observe potential Field candidates through the lens of scholarly, engineering, scientific, and professional communities.
c.focus: Recognizable communities of practice, disciplinary terminology, professional domains, and recurring knowledge identities.

d.description: Observe potential Field candidates through the lens of persistent or emerging research activity and scholarly ecosystems.
d.focus: Research areas, recurring scholarly communities, publication ecosystems, conferences, journals, and emerging research domains.

e.description: Observe potential Field candidates through the lens of academic and research institutional structures.
e.focus: Schools, departments, degree programs, majors, laboratories, research centers, and persistent institutional research areas.

f.description: Observe potential Field candidates through the lens of professional, engineering, occupational, technological, and industrial practice.
f.focus: Professional domains, engineering practices, technological domains, occupational structures, applied knowledge areas, and industrially recognizable Fields.
